title: Two cultures
hook: raising children between Punjab and wherever you live
tomorrow: Maya's family looks nothing like Simran's. is there room for them?

segments.voice: Yesterday, family Nitnem: Sohila at bedtime, Harjit asleep by the second hymn, and Bebe reading on. Pray together. Fateh stayed awake for all of it, and the next morning he had a question.

Some kids have two lunchboxes in their head: the one they bring to school, and the one they'd never bring. Over breakfast, Fateh pushes his Gurmukhi workbook away. Nobody at school learns Punjabi, he says. Why do I have to? Massi looks at Simran. Simran, who leaves for college in a year and has been asking herself the same thing lately, puts down her tea and takes the question seriously.
screen: `TWO LUNCHBOXES IN ONE HEAD.` → `WHY DO I HAVE TO LEARN PUNJABI?` → `SIMRAN TAKES IT SERIOUSLY.`

segments.voice: Gurmukhi is the script the Guru Granth Sahib is written in, and tradition credits Guru Angad with shaping it and teaching it. So the letters in Fateh's workbook are the door to reading the Gurus in their own words, at Bebe's kitchen table or anywhere on earth. That's Simran's first answer. Her second: you don't have to pick a lunchbox. Two cultures, Punjab and California, can both be home, the way the Granth itself holds the verses of Guru Nanak beside saints like Kabir and Farid, from other backgrounds. And the last two weeks were full of two worlds meeting. Rounds walked as a map for two. One light in two bodies. Patience at home after a fight. Tea poured for a daughter-in-law first. A living room turned small sangat. Bebe reading while Harjit snored. None of that is only Punjab and none of it is only California. It's a family carrying something old into a new place, a word at a time. Fateh pulls the workbook back. Fine, he says. But you have to learn one too. Simran agrees. Her letter for the day is the one that starts his name.
screen: `GURMUKHI: THE GRANTH'S SCRIPT.` · `YOU DON'T HAVE TO PICK A LUNCHBOX.` · `TWO WEEKS OF TWO WORLDS MEETING.` · `A WORD AT A TIME.` · then, large: `TWO WORLDS.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write, by hand, one word from a language your family carries, or one word you'd want passed on to someone younger. Write it slowly, letter by letter, the way Fateh traces his workbook. Then rest your hand on the page for the sit.
Two cultures. Raising children between Punjab and wherever you live, carrying the Gurus' words into a new home.
Two worlds, one family, and a workbook pulled back across the table. Two weeks, done.
